text: It does a fair job of presenting both sides of whether or not convicted child murderer Lucy Letby is guilty of the crimes that sent to prison for life. Previously unseen police footage is the main reason to watch.
The film is an interesting and uncomfortable document of whose privacy is deemed important in a case like this.

With no new revelations pertaining to the case, the main talking point from this documentary looks likely to be the footage of the arrests. Bar the noise and the rubbernecking﻿, there is little of real substance to add about the harrowing case.
Given the use of AI to "create" characters making assertions about Lucy and the case, this feels like an exercise in hoodwinking.
This film had all the excellent footage (including police interviews) and the exclusive sit-downs you might want.
This should not exist. It is simply picking over long-clean bones for bad reasons: poking a terrible bruise for the pleasure of onlookers.
The Investigation of Lucy Letby does not compare in its attention to detail, preferring a broader-brush, more emotive telling of the story.

...it suffers from the current irritating documentary trend of having contributors talking in the present tense about past events. But it does give a fascinating insight into the police investigation and their treatment of their chief suspect.

... watching a Netflix true crime documentary like this is tough. It’s about the untimely and shocking deaths of many newborn babies, which IS a hard watch. And it is so very easy to get angry at Lucy Letby for not reacting as you may...
